prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE polished, extremely readable, publication-quality research architecture image for a professor presentation about RACE-RL. The attached image is a LAYOUT AND VISUAL-STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: a small input graph on left, one large neural agent in the middle, compact action pictograms, an isometric chiplet environment on right, and two long feedback arrows. Replace its subject with this project's actual algorithm. White opaque background. Extra-wide landscape 3:1 aspect ratio, high resolution approximately 3600x1200. Thin charcoal panel boundaries, crisp navy/teal flow arrows, restrained yellow highlights behind only key headings, colored neurons, neat orthogonal feedback routes. Large Times New Roman labels. Sparse text, no paragraphs or bullet lists, icons and diagrams occupy most of the image.

EXACT STRUCTURE LEFT TO RIGHT:
1. Left narrow input panel, title "State". Inside: a tiny CNN dependency graph (colored circles connected by arrows) above a small 2x2 hardware-mesh graph; a few dashed placement/transfer links connect the two graphs. A highlighted edge indicates data-transfer attribution, NOT a hardware fault. NO dimension numbers or feature tables.
2. Large center panel, title "Single RACE-RL Agent". Inside this SINGLE enclosing agent: a small heterogeneous graph/message-passing visual labelled "Relational Encoder" on the left, a substantial colored fully-connected neural network illustration labelled "Joint Actor" on the right. One thick short arrow connects encoder to actor. Do not make two independent agents. Tiny method label "REINFORCE" along the bottom of this enclosing panel.
3. A slim action section labelled "Complete Action". Use only three compact visual motifs below it: a tiny variable chip grid labelled "1–16"; a cuboid divided into tiles; two dependent operator dots A and B moving together to a new chip. A small bracket below these motifs labelled "Coupled Edit" shows these are all ONE finished action. Only ONE forward arrow from the complete action section into the environment. Do not draw environment evaluations between the motifs or between A and B edits.
4. Right panel title "Environment" highlighted pale yellow. Inside: a clean isometric 2x2 compute chiplet mesh on a flat interposer, with visible orthogonal mesh traces and directional data-transfer arrows. Exactly ONE small external DRAM component outside the mesh, linked to chiplet c0 only. One compute chiplet can have a simple enlarged/cutaway memory-to-PE mini-stack labelled only "GB", "LB", "RF", "PE", with a small side box "ACC" branching from LB. This is a diagram, not a real silicon photograph. At bottom of environment, three small meter bars grouped under one label "PPA". Keep diagram legible, no dense wiring, no faults, no red crosses.

FEEDBACK:
Top outer blue arrow begins at the Environment, travels left above all panels, and enters the TOP of the Single RACE-RL Agent; label only "Reward".
Bottom outer blue arrow begins at Environment, travels left below all panels and enters the BOTTOM of the left State panel; label only "Next State".
These long feedback arrows must have unambiguous arrowheads at the correct destinations and no crossing with the forward path.

SCIENTIFIC INVARIANTS: one shared Encoder+Joint Actor, one complete coupled action then ONE environment evaluation then reward/state. No Teacher Model, no Student Model, no knowledge distillation, no DQN, no PPO, no critic, no fault tolerance and no link direction decision menu. No predictions of PPA inside agent. No two-DRAM system, no memory chiplets. Four chiplets shown only as illustrative environment; action count explicitly ranges 1–16. No invented accuracy, speedup, physical PPA numbers. Avoid extra labels, captions, footnotes, decorative gadgets, tiny text, line crossings, gradients or clutter. Every item well inside 5 percent image margins. Main image should look like a journal architecture figure, close to the reference's horizontal organization, using pictures instead of text-filled boxes.
interpretation: Conceptual research architecture. Neural-layer/node counts, highlighted links, four chiplets, PPA bar levels and interposer geometry are illustrations, not literal network sizes, faults, selected designs, results or physical layout. Actual compute count is selected from 1–16. One encoder/joint actor and one complete action precede environment feedback; REINFORCE updates at episode end.
